name: Don Quijote · Gustave Doré
description: Edición literaria a columna y media con glosas al margen y láminas de Doré · A column-and-a-half literary edition with margin glosses and Doré's plates
credits: Cervantes · Ormsby · Doré · Project Gutenberg · Wikimedia Commons

es.title: El ingenioso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha
Que trata de la condición y ejercicio del famoso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha
Que trata de la primera salida que de su tierra hizo el ingenioso don Quijote
Donde se cuenta la graciosa manera que tuvo don Quijote en armarse caballero
De lo que le sucedió a nuestro caballero cuando salió de la venta
Donde se prosigue la narración de la desgracia de nuestro caballero
Del donoso y grande escrutinio que el cura y el barbero hicieron en la librería de nuestro ingenioso hidalgo
De la segunda salida de nuestro buen caballero don Quijote de la Mancha
Del buen suceso que el valeroso don Quijote tuvo en la espantable y jamás imaginada aventura de los molinos de viento, con otros sucesos dignos de felice recordación
Donde se concluye y da fin a la estupenda batalla que el gallardo vizcaíno y el valiente manchego tuvieron
De lo que más le avino a don Quijote con el vizcaíno, y del peligro en que se vio con una turba de yangüeses
De lo que le sucedió a don Quijote con unos cabreros
De lo que contó un cabrero a los que estaban con don Quijote
Donde se da fin al cuento de la pastora Marcela, con otros sucesos
Donde se ponen los versos desesperados del difunto pastor, con otros no esperados sucesos

en.title: The Ingenious Gentleman Don Quixote of La Mancha
Which treats of the character and pursuits of the famous gentleman Don Quixote of La Mancha
Which treats of the first sally the ingenious Don Quixote made from home
Wherein is related the droll way in which Don Quixote had himself dubbed a knight
Of what happened to our knight when he left the inn
In which the narrative of our knight’s mishap is continued
Of the diverting and important scrutiny which the curate and the barber made in the library of our ingenious gentleman
Of the second sally of our worthy knight Don Quixote of La Mancha
Of the good fortune which the valiant Don Quixote had in the terrible and undreamt-of adventure of the windmills, with other occurrences worthy to be fitly recorded
In which is concluded and finished the terrific battle between the gallant Biscayan and the valiant Manchegan
Of the pleasant discourse that passed between Don Quixote and his squire Sancho Panza
What befell Don Quixote with certain goatherds
Of what a goatherd related to those with Don Quixote
In which is ended the story of the shepherdess Marcela, with other incidents
Wherein are inserted the despairing verses of the dead shepherd, together with other incidents not looked for

resources.caption: «El pie de aquella montaña es el lugar donde él mandó que le enterrasen.»

resources.altText: «El pie de aquella montaña es el lugar donde él mandó que le enterrasen.»

resources.caption: «Cerraron la sepultura con una gruesa peña, en tanto que se acababa una losa.»
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; grabado por H. Pisan. Dominio público, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: «Cerraron la sepultura con una gruesa peña, en tanto que se acababa una losa.»

resources.caption: «Murió a manos del rigor de una esquiva hermosa ingrata, con quien su imperio dilata la tiranía de su amor.»
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; grabado por H. Pisan. Dominio público, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: «Murió a manos del rigor de una esquiva hermosa ingrata, con quien su imperio dilata la tiranía de su amor.»

resources.caption: “A world of disorderly notions, picked out of his books, crowded into his imagination.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “A world of disorderly notions, picked out of his books, crowded into his imagination.”

resources.caption: “He next proceeded to inspect his hack.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “He next proceeded to inspect his hack.”

resources.caption: “At the door were standing two young women.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “At the door were standing two young women.”

resources.caption: “Putting one end in his mouth, they poured the wine into him through the other.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Putting one end in his mouth, they poured the wine into him through the other.”

resources.caption: “With a graceful bearing he began pacing to and fro before the trough.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “With a graceful bearing he began pacing to and fro before the trough.”

resources.caption: “After it, with his own sword, a slap on the shoulder, all the while muttering between his teeth.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “After it, with his own sword, a slap on the shoulder, all the while muttering between his teeth.”

resources.caption: “One of the ladies girded on his sword.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “One of the ladies girded on his sword.”

resources.caption: “Discourteous knight, it ill becomes you to assail one who cannot defend himself.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Discourteous knight, it ill becomes you to assail one who cannot defend himself.”

resources.caption: “Coming up to him, he seized his lance, and having broken it in pieces, began to belabour him.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Coming up to him, he seized his lance, and having broken it in pieces, began to belabour him.”

resources.caption: “He again tried to rise, but was unable.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “He again tried to rise, but was unable.”

resources.caption: “The peasant set him on his ass and gathered up the arms.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “The peasant set him on his ass and gathered up the arms.”

resources.caption: “Open, your worships, to Señor Baldwin and to Señor the Marquis of Mantua, who comes badly wounded.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Open, your worships, to Señor Baldwin and to Señor the Marquis of Mantua, who comes badly wounded.”

resources.caption: “The peasant waited until it was a little later that the belaboured gentleman might not be seen riding in such a miserable trim.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “The peasant waited until it was a little later that the belaboured gentleman might not be seen riding in such a miserable trim.”

resources.caption: “The housekeeper burned them that night in the yard.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “The housekeeper burned them that night in the yard.”

resources.caption: “So much did he say, so much did he persuade and promise, that the poor clown made up his mind to go with him.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “So much did he say, so much did he persuade and promise, that the poor clown made up his mind to go with him.”

resources.caption: “After a little while he made off, flying through the roof, and left the house full of smoke.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “After a little while he made off, flying through the roof, and left the house full of smoke.”

resources.caption: “A slight breeze sprang up, and the great sails began to move; at Rocinante’s fullest gallop he charged.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “A slight breeze sprang up, and the great sails began to move; at Rocinante’s fullest gallop he charged.”

resources.caption: “Sancho hastened to his assistance as fast as his ass could go.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Sancho hastened to his assistance as fast as his ass could go.”

resources.caption: “Helping him to rise, he got him up again on Rocinante, whose shoulder was half out.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Helping him to rise, he got him up again on Rocinante, whose shoulder was half out.”

resources.caption: “The ladies in the coach implored him to grant them the great grace of sparing their squire’s life.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “The ladies in the coach implored him to grant them the great grace of sparing their squire’s life.”

resources.caption: “Daylight failed them close by the huts of some goatherds, so they determined to pass the night there.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Daylight failed them close by the huts of some goatherds, so they determined to pass the night there.”

resources.caption: “Happy the age, happy the time, to which the ancients gave the name of golden.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Happy the age, happy the time, to which the ancients gave the name of golden.”

resources.caption: “Gathering some leaves of rosemary, he chewed them and mixed them with a little salt, and applying them to the ear he secured them firmly with a bandage.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Gathering some leaves of rosemary, he chewed them and mixed them with a little salt, and applying them to the ear he secured them firmly with a bandage.”

resources.caption: “Sancho Panza settled himself between Rocinante and his ass, and slept, not like a lover who had been discarded, but like a man who had been soundly kicked.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “Sancho Panza settled himself between Rocinante and his ass, and slept, not like a lover who had been discarded, but like a man who had been soundly kicked.”

resources.caption: “The foot of that mountain is the place where he ordered them to bury him.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “The foot of that mountain is the place where he ordered them to bury him.”

resources.caption: “They closed the grave with a heavy stone until a slab was ready.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “They closed the grave with a heavy stone until a slab was ready.”

resources.caption: “In death a victim to disdain. Ungrateful, cruel, coy, and fair, was she that drove him to despair.”
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; engraved by H. Pisan. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
resources.altText: “In death a victim to disdain. Ungrateful, cruel, coy, and fair, was she that drove him to despair.”

resources.caption: «Sancho Panza se acomodó entre Rocinante y su jumento, y durmió, no como enamorado desfavorecido, sino como hombre molido a coces.»
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; grabado por H. Pisan. Dominio público, Wikimedia Commons.

resources.caption: «El pie de aquella montaña es el lugar donde él mandó que le enterrasen.»
resources.note: Gustave Doré, 1863; grabado por H. Pisan. Dominio público, Wikimedia Commons.

resources.caption: «Cerraron la sepultura con una gruesa peña, en tanto que se acababa una losa.»

resources.caption: «Murió a manos del rigor de una esquiva hermosa ingrata, con quien su imperio dilata la tiranía de su amor.»
